notes: Vanilla Broke Protocol ships no remote command channel: no RCON, no HTTP/REST admin API, and no server-console command parser. The official setup page (brokeprotocol.com/bp/) names only files to edit - settings.json, server_info.txt, announcements.txt, groups.json - started with Server.bat (Windows) or ./start.sh (Linux) on UDP 5557 and 5558, and the official wiki Server-Administration page adds whitelist.txt; neither mentions a console, a command, or a remote admin port. The older How-to-host-Server wiki page still describes a pre-1.0 file scheme (Settings.txt, Admin_list.txt, Ban_list.txt, Start.sh/Stop.sh) that groups.json and the in-game admin tools have since replaced - treat that page as out of date rather than as evidence of a plain-text ban file. Moderation in vanilla is done in-game by a player holding admin permissions: the v1.01 Admin Update added the Player Records menu (last 500 connections, view player info, submit bans even after the player left) and the group/permission manager backed by groups.json; bans are LiteDB records - the official Game API Reference documents a BrokeProtocol.LiteDB.Ban class - so no banList is recorded. The official CommandHandler doc confirms the shape of the command system: commands are registered by plugins and are invoked IN-GAME as chat commands by a player (the first parameter is always the calling ShPlayer, e.g. /ban "John Smith" "Some Reason"), gated by a namespace.command permission in groups.json - they are not console input, and the Steam thread about "offline console commands" resolves to exactly that, adding your name to the owner group in groups.json. GameSource/Commands.cs, the vanilla registration site, registers only demo commands (ExampleArgs, ExampleTest, ExampleDiscord, CoinFlip, SlowMo) - no kick, ban, say or player list. Third-party plugins change this but are not the base server: xiluisx/ConsoleCommands exists specifically to "allow you to use simple commands in the Broke Protocol Console" and adds AddGroup, Ban, BanInfo, BanList, Give, Groups, Help, ItemList, Online, Say, Teleport and UnBan; BPEssentials/Core adds a broader moderation suite as in-game chat commands. If a managed server is known to run one of those plugins, that plugin's command set - not this file - is what to send. Confidence is low because this is an argument from absence: no source states outright that Broke Protocol has no RCON/REST/console, it is inferred from the official hosting page, the official wiki, the official command API and the existence of a plugin whose whole purpose is adding console commands. No separate dedicated-server Steam app exists; the server is the game build itself (app 696370, the id Steam uses for BROKE PROTOCOL: Online City RPG).
